think.script:
Welcome to the Foot Bridge!

[ON SCREEN: Bridge board]

Last night the Smudge snapped Gus's rope rail, so nobody can cross to Eastside. The board right under me has five bridge jobs. Each one uses today's math.

[ON SCREEN: Two posts]

Here's the first puzzle. Gus has two tall posts at the ends of his bridge. The north post is 6 feet 5 inches tall. The tag on the south post says 79 inches. Which post is taller, and by how many inches?

[ON SCREEN: The big question]

One height has two units, feet and inches. The other has only inches. So how do you compare them? Don't wait for me to show you. First, build a foot on Gus's ruler, so you know how many inches make a foot. Then try the post puzzle your own way, and write down how you did it. On the Learn tab, the Math Crew will show you two ways, and you can see if one matches yours.

board.title: North: 6 ft 5 in · South: 79 in
board.sub: Write both heights the same way. Which post is taller?

board.title: Which post is taller, and by how much?

learn.script:
Let's find out which post is taller, two ways.

[ON SCREEN: Board: The posts]

[DRAW: point to the north post's row, 6 | 5. Write 79 in beside the empty row for the south post.]

The north post is 6 feet 5 inches. The south post is 79 inches. They're written two different ways, so we can't compare them yet. We need them in the same unit.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Two ways]

[DRAW: fill in Atlas's blanks as you say them, then Felix's.]

Atlas changes the south post to feet and inches. He splits 79 with a number bond: 72 and 7. 72 inches is 6 feet. So the south post is 6 feet 7 inches, and 7 inches is 2 more than 5. Felix changes the north post to inches instead. 6 times 12 is 72, plus 5 is 77 inches. 79 minus 77 is 2. Both ways say the south post, by 2 inches!

[ON SCREEN: Live: The Rope Ruler]

[DO: tap the 1 ft piece 3 times. Tap the 1 in piece 10 times. Point to the number sentence. Type 10 in the empty circle of the number bond and tap Check.]

Now Rosa's rope, 46 inches. On the Rope Ruler, I lay whole feet first: 12, 24, 36. One more foot would make 48. Too long! So I fill in with inches: 37, 38, all the way to 46. In the bond, 36 inches and 10 inches. 3 feet 10 inches.

Remember, 12 inches make a foot, not 10. Now build Rosa's rope on your page.

do.script:
Now watch me solve three. Pause any time.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 1]

[DRAW: write 3 | 7 in row 1 and 1 | 8 in row 2. Add down: 4 | 15. Cross out 15, write 3, and add 1 to the feet: 5 | 3.]

3 feet 7 inches plus 1 foot 8 inches. Feet: 4. Inches: 15. That's more than a foot, so I trade 12 inches for 1 foot. 5 feet 3 inches.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 2]

[DRAW: write 4 | 3 on top and 2 | 7 under it. Cross out 4, write 3. Cross out 3 in, write 15. Subtract each column: 1 | 8.]

4 feet 3 inches minus 2 feet 7 inches. 3 minus 7 won't work. So I trade 1 foot for 12 inches: 3 feet 15 inches. 15 minus 7 is 8. 3 minus 2 is 1. 1 foot 8 inches. Felix checks it in inches: 51 minus 31 is 20, and 20 inches is 1 foot 8 inches. Same!

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 3]

[DRAW: under 3 yd write 9 ft. Add the 2 ft: 11 ft. Write 11 × 12 = 132 in, then + 5 in = 137 in.]

3 yards 2 feet 5 inches, all in inches. One step at a time. 3 yards is 9 feet. 9 feet and 2 more feet make 11 feet. Each foot is 12 inches, so 11 feet is 132 inches. Add the 5 inches: 137 inches.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Spot the mistake]

[DRAW: circle 3 ft 3 in. Write 13 in = 12 in + 1 in, then 3 ft 1 in.]

Is this right? Someone treated inches like tens and ones. But a foot is 12 inches, not 10. 13 inches is 12 and 1, so it's 3 feet 1 inch. Watch for that on the rope order!

wrap.script:
Look how far you came!

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]

Today you compared, added and subtracted lengths with feet and inches. You can work in feet and inches and trade 12 inches for a foot, or change it all to inches first. Both give the same answer.

[ON SCREEN: The banner]

And the Smudge's banner? 2 feet 15 inches is 39 inches, but 3 feet 5 inches is 41 inches. They don't match! 15 inches is 1 foot and 3 inches, so the banner should say 3 feet 3 inches. And you chased the Smudge all the way to Eastside!

[ON SCREEN: Next time]

Next time we walk into the General Store in Eastside, where 16 ounces make a pound. See you there, explorers!
